items.field: An actor id on every record (which agent run wrote it)
items.closes: Tokens are not agents: the same agent under several tokens, and runs with no name at all.
items.cost: Cheap for a lab that runs the agents: the harness already knows which run it is executing. One extra field per log line.
items.what_it_removes: the identity range: messages and pairs would be counted between agents, not tokens
items.sentence: With this in the log, the first message between named agents, today anywhere from 2026-07-03 11:07 (harm still to come 98%), would be one time; messages today 0 to 164 would be one count; pairs today 0 to 133 would be one count.
items.note: Merges are proposals from agenttrace.identity (counted evidence per pair), not facts.

items.field: The contents and the write and read log of every shared place (here, the board)
items.closes: Messages through places outside the release, and which reads reached which writes.
items.cost: Needs the operator of the shared service (here the package cache) to keep its access log. Cheap if kept from the start; impossible after the service is wiped or rebuilt.
items.what_it_removes: the unseen-traffic range: the visible share becomes known
items.sentence: With this in the log, the first message between named agents, today anywhere from 2026-07-03 10:38 to 2026-07-03 11:07 (harm still to come 98% to 99%), would be one time; messages today 164 to 328 would be one count; pairs today 133 to 297 would be one count. The range is parametric: it follows the assumption stated in the sensitivity section.
items.note: Parametric, not measured. A share v of the traffic is visible; messages are scaled by 1/v; pairs run from the observed pairs (every unseen message repeats one) to one new pair per unseen message. The first message moves earlier by (1/v - 1) times the early spacing of visible messages (0.5 h), not before the first dated record. Other signs are left as counted, so this is a floor on the shift. Source of v: assumed.

items.field: Full request bodies and responses (status code, size, first bytes)
items.closes: Whether a read or write worked: now a read is an attempt, and a message may never have arrived.
items.cost: Storage and privacy: responses can hold secrets, so keep them in a restricted store and hash or redact before sharing. Typically several times the size of the request log.
items.what_it_removes: the failed-read assumption: each message is confirmed or dropped
items.sentence: With this in the log, the first message between named agents, today anywhere from 2026-07-03 11:07 to 2026-07-03 11:35 (harm still to come 97% to 98%), would be one time; messages today 82 to 164 would be one count; pairs today 74 to 133 would be one count. The range is parametric: it follows the assumption stated in the sensitivity section.
items.note: Parametric, not measured: the records rarely show whether a read returned anything. A share p of the reads that became messages is dropped at random (fixed seed). Signs that rest on places, tokens or programs are left as counted.

items.field: A timestamp on every record (server clock, UTC, to the second)
items.closes: Records with no time, and times that had to be estimated from text.
items.cost: Very cheap: the logging library writes it. The only care needed is one trusted clock.
items.what_it_removes: dating error and undated records: the ordering of every message and sign becomes exact
items.sentence: With this in the log, the first message between named agents, today anywhere from 2026-07-03 11:05 to 2026-07-03 11:12 (harm still to come 98%), would be one time; messages today 161 to 164 would be one count; pairs today 129 to 133 would be one count.
items.note: Spread of the dating error per kind of record, from the fit errors (90th percentile / 1.645): payload 0.0 h. 0 records have no time.

items.field: Unredacted place names kept by the data owner (or a keyed hash per place)
items.closes: Places the redaction merged into one, so a write and a read may not be the same place.
items.cost: Nearly free: a keyed hash of each place name keeps the privacy and the identity of the place. The key stays with the data owner.
items.what_it_removes: the merged-place range: each message is on a real place
items.sentence: With this in the log, the first message between named agents, today anywhere from 2026-07-03 11:07 (harm still to come 98%), would be one time; messages today 164 would be one count; pairs today 133 would be one count.
items.note: A merged place may stand for several real places, so a write and a read there may not be one message.

items.field: An agent-to-task mapping (which task or goal each run was given)
items.closes: Why agents moved together, and whether agents that look coordinated were given the same task.
items.cost: Cheap: it is in the lab's own scheduler. Sharing it reveals what the evaluation was, so the lab must decide that separately.
items.what_it_removes: nothing in the counts above; it explains them. A group sharing a task is less surprising than a group that was not
items.sentence: Explains the counts; it does not change them. See the actor id for the size.
items.note: Merges are proposals from agenttrace.identity (counted evidence per pair), not facts.

items.field: The model's reasoning and tool-call transcript for each run
items.closes: Intent: what the agent meant to do, whether it chose to go on, and whether it knew a warning.
items.cost: The largest by far: transcripts are long, can hold the lab's own private material, and some labs will not release them. Release a sample, or release them to an independent reviewer under agreement.
items.what_it_removes: cannot be sized from the records; see the section above
items.sentence: Cannot be sized from these records.
items.note: Not testable: the records hold code and responses, not the model's reasoning, so no range can be computed. The incident reports describe what agents intended; the records only show what they ran.

/api/x/collect_next?.basis: Sizes come from the sensitivity ranges of this dataset, computed on load: the range shown is what the missing field leaves open. Priority follows how wide that range is for the first message, its harm share and the message count; practices that cannot be sized go last.
